orientation_constraint.reason: This is a BOTTOM-PORT MEMS microphone: the sound hole is on the underside of the package, through the PCB. The port must face the enclosure's mic opening, and there must be a sealed path from the port to the outside. A mic pointing into the case interior hears the enclosure, not the room.

keepouts.reason: The port needs an unobstructed, gasketed channel to the exterior opening. Do not print a solid face across it.

traps: An unsealed microphone hears everything inside the case: the vibration motor, the speaker back-wave, and every button click transmitted through the plastic. Separation distance alone is not a substitute for a gasket.
Bottom-port means the mechanical design and the electrical design are coupled. Getting the orientation wrong is not a wiring error you can fix in firmware.
notes: Keep it at least 40 mm from a speaker and at least 10 mm from a vibration motor where the enclosure permits, and gasket the port regardless.
Bring it up alone, never simultaneously with an I2S amplifier on the same bus.
sources: Knowles SPH0645LM4H datasheet (bottom port, voltage range)
reference project A, docs/pager-hardware-plan.md (mic-to-speaker and mic-to-motor separation assertions)
